  "text": "Elias kept his shoulder against the cellar door. Ada picked up the key without touching its teeth.

“Venn?” his wife called.

From below came the scrape of a chair. “Ask her what she put under the door.”

Ada looked at the sleeve in her hand. It belonged to the constable’s coat. Its cuff was dry now, and its torn edge showed a neat row of stitches.

The constable stared at his bare arm. “That’s not mine.”

A second knock came from the cellar. This one sounded close to the floor.

Venn’s wife took the key from Ada and held it over the match flame. Water beaded along its shaft, then fell in slow drops onto the tile. Each drop left a dark mark shaped like a small hand.

“Open the back door,” she said.

Elias did not move. “What about Venn?”

“He knows the way out.”

Below them, the chair scraped again. Venn began to laugh, but the sound broke off when the constable opened the kitchen door. Cold air swept through the room. The marks on the floor drew together and slipped across the threshold into the yard.

Only then did Elias step away from the cellar.

Ada heard the bolt slide back. Venn’s wife caught her hand and pulled her outside before the door could open. They stood beside the rain barrel, listening to footsteps cross the kitchen.

One set stopped at the open back door. The other continued down the hall.

“Which one was Venn?” Ada asked.

His wife closed her fingers around the key. “I’m waiting to hear.”"
